faqs.q: Why do character counters disagree about emoji?
faqs.a: Because a character can be counted four ways: as one grapheme cluster (what a reader sees), as Unicode code points, as UTF-16 code units (the browser/JavaScript length), or as UTF-8 bytes. One emoji can be 1, 2 or more code points, 2 UTF-16 units and 4 or more bytes. This tool shows all four counts and names the method behind each.

faqs.q: Are the platform limits guaranteed?

Treat the presets as planning guidance and trust the counter inside the app you post to for the final word.

faqs.q: Why does an SMS shrink from 160 to 70 characters?
faqs.a: A plain SMS uses the GSM-7 alphabet at 160 characters per segment. Add any character outside that set — Urdu or Arabic script, many emoji — and the whole message is encoded as Unicode (UCS-2) at 70 characters per segment, so it splits into more segments sooner than the headline number suggests.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Character Counter and the Word Counter?
faqs.a: The Word Counter answers how much you wrote: words, sentences, paragraphs, reading time and your most repeated words. This Character Counter answers whether it fits and how it is counted: exact characters by four methods and live checks against platform limits. Each page links to the other.

faqs.q: Is Base64 encryption?
faqs.a: No. Base64 is encoding, not encryption. Anyone who has the Base64 string can decode it without a key, so never use Base64 to protect passwords, tokens or secrets.

faqs.q: What is URL-safe Base64?
faqs.a: URL-safe Base64 replaces + with - and / with _, and usually drops the trailing = padding. It carries the same data in an alphabet that is safer inside URLs and filenames.

faqs.q: Why did my Base64 fail to decode?
faqs.a: Usually a character is missing, extra or changed, padding is in the wrong place, or the decoded bytes are binary data rather than UTF-8 text. This tool explains the specific problem instead of silently showing garbled output.

faqs.q: Can I encode a file to Base64 here?

faqs.q: Does a clean slug guarantee better Google ranking?

faqs.q: Which stop words are removed?

faqs.q: Is my text uploaded anywhere?

faqs.q: What happens with repeated keys and very large numbers?
faqs.a: Standard JSON.parse keeps only the last value when a key repeats, and whole numbers beyond 2^53−1 can lose precision. Keep identifiers and large counters as strings when exact digits matter.

faqs.q: How does this calculator count the days between two dates?

faqs.a: Most analytics tools are case-sensitive, so Facebook and facebook count as two sources, and one channel written three ways becomes three report rows. Use lowercase, hyphens or underscores instead of spaces, and the exact same spelling every time.

faqs.q: Can I put personal data in UTM values?
faqs.a: Never put names, email addresses or other personal data in UTM values. Links are forwarded, logged and pasted into chats, so anything inside a URL travels. Label the campaign, never the person.

faqs.q: Does a correct UTM link guarantee correct reporting?
faqs.a: No. Analytics must be installed on the landing page; consent mode or blockers can prevent recording; redirects can drop the query string; and some platforms strip parameters when a link is shared onward. Tag external links only.

faqs.q: Is anything uploaded?
faqs.a: No. The link is built in your browser tab with encodeURIComponent, and saved presets stay on this device. Nothing is uploaded, stored on a server or shared.

facts: UTMs do not guarantee attribution — test the final link

faqs.q: Why show pixels as well as characters?
faqs.a: Letters have different widths (WWW is wider than iii), so the same character count can take up different space. Google truncates closer to display width than to a fixed character number. The pixel figure here is an approximation from canvas measurement and is labelled approximate.

faqs.q: What length is good, and does it help ranking?
faqs.a: Only display guidance can be given: about 30–60 characters for a title and 120–160 for a description on desktop, less on mobile. Fitting a band makes truncation less likely; it does not improve ranking, and Google sets no fixed limit.

faqs.q: Will Google show exactly what I typed?
faqs.a: Often not. Google frequently rewrites titles and replaces descriptions with a snippet from page content, varying by query and device. No checker can guarantee display or ranking. Put important words first and treat any preview as a writing aid.

faqs.q: Should I add meta keywords?
faqs.a: No. Google does not use the meta keywords tag for ranking. This checker deliberately ignores it.

faqs.q: Is anything uploaded?
faqs.a: No. Counting and pixel measurement run in your browser tab. Nothing is uploaded, stored or shared.

facts: Runs: in your browser (canvas pixel-width estimate)
Desktop + mobile SERP previews for title and description
Google often rewrites both — guidance only, never a ranking promise

faqs.q: Why does Instagram remove my blank lines?
faqs.a: Instagram's composer strips empty lines and trailing spaces when text is published, so paragraphs typed with blank lines between them collapse into one block. A line that contains an invisible character is not empty, so it survives.

faqs.q: What character does this tool put on blank lines?
faqs.a: By default the Braille Pattern Blank U+2800, a real character that renders as blank space in fonts that support it. You can instead choose a visible dot divider (·) if you prefer a separator readers can see.

faqs.q: Is my caption uploaded anywhere?
faqs.a: No. The conversion happens in your browser tab. Your text is not uploaded, stored on a server or shared by this tool, and closing the tab forgets everything.

faqs.q: Will the line breaks always survive on Instagram?
faqs.a: No tool can promise that. Instagram can change how it treats these characters at any time, a few fonts show a box instead of a blank, and screen readers may read the blank character aloud. Check the preview after pasting before you publish.

faqs.q: Do the invisible characters count toward Instagram's limits?
faqs.a: Yes. Instagram commonly limits captions to 2,200 characters and bios to 150, and spacer characters count toward those numbers. The tool shows the copied length so you can check before pasting.

faqs.q: Does this work for bios and comments too?
faqs.a: The same trick works anywhere Instagram collapses blank lines: captions, bios and comments. Story text and some Reels fields behave differently, so test there first.

facts: Adds clean line breaks for Instagram captions and bios
Instagram can change limits/rendering — check after pasting

faqs.q: How does the image compressor work?
faqs.a: It re-encodes JPG, PNG and WebP images in your browser at the quality you choose and shows the size before and after, so you can balance file size against how the image looks.

faqs.q: Is my image uploaded?

faqs.q: Why did the compressed file come out larger?
faqs.a: If the original was already very small, re-encoding can make it bigger. The tool tells you honestly when that happens — keep your original in that case, or try a lower quality setting.

faqs.q: Is it free?
faqs.a: Yes. It is free with no sign-up and no watermark.

facts: JPG, PNG and WebP with before/after sizes
Your image is not uploaded; no watermark

faqs.a: Two jobs: merge several PDF files into one, and convert JPG or PNG images into a single PDF. Pick your files, arrange the order, and download the result.

faqs.q: Are my PDFs uploaded?

faqs.q: Is it free?

faqs.q: Any limits?
faqs.a: Very large files are limited by your device's memory. This tool merges and converts; it does not edit PDF text or run OCR — for text from a scanned page, use the Image to Text tool.

facts: Merge PDFs; convert JPG/PNG images to one PDF

faqs.q: Is this audio to text converter free?
faqs.a: Yes. It is free with no sign-up and no per-minute charge. Transcription runs on your own device in your browser.

faqs.q: Is my audio uploaded anywhere?
faqs.a: No. Your file is decoded and transcribed inside your browser tab. The only download is a one-time copy of the compact Whisper speech model (about 40 MB) from a public model library, which your browser then caches.

faqs.q: Which audio formats can I use?
faqs.a: MP3, WAV, M4A and MP4 work well, plus any audio or video format your browser itself can play. If a file cannot be decoded, the tool says so plainly instead of guessing.

faqs.q: How accurate is the transcript?
faqs.a: It is at its best with short, clear recordings: one speaker, little background noise, roughly a few minutes at a time. Long, noisy or multi-speaker recordings will contain more mistakes, and names and technical words are usually the first to go wrong. Always proofread before relying on the text.

faqs.q: Can I get subtitles for a video?
faqs.a: Yes. After transcribing, download the .srt or .vtt export — both carry the model's timestamps as subtitle cues. If you edit the transcript text, the subtitle export falls back to one cue holding the edited text.

faqs.q: Does it work offline?
faqs.a: After the first visit, the speech model is cached by your browser, so transcription keeps working without an internet connection. The very first transcription needs to be online to fetch the model.

faqs.q: Which countries is Muse AI available in?
faqs.a: Based on Meta's own announcements checked on 10 October 2026: the United States (launch, 8 September 2026) and Canada (confirmed 29 September 2026). Meta has announced no other launch country and no launch dates for anywhere else.

faqs.q: Is Muse AI available in Pakistan or India?
faqs.a: Not yet. Meta has announced only the United States and Canada (checked 10 October 2026) and has published no date for Pakistan or India. Sign in at muse.ai to see whether a waitlist opens for your region.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Muse and Meta AI?
faqs.a: Meta AI is the assistant inside Meta's apps (WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger) — you ask it something and it answers. Muse is Meta's newer personal agent that can take a goal, research across sources, plan steps, and work on tasks for you. They are two different products.

faqs.q: Is Muse free?
faqs.a: Meta's official FAQ says Muse is available for free with a usage limit. If you hit that limit you can upgrade to a paid subscription for a higher limit or wait for the free limit to refresh. Meta had not published exact paid-plan amounts on its public pages as of 10 October 2026.

faqs.q: What are Muse tokens? Can I buy '1 billion tokens'?
faqs.a: Tokens are units of usage — they measure how much work Muse does for you, like minutes on a phone plan. They are not money and not cryptocurrency. Third-party blogs claim '1 billion token' invite codes, but Meta's official pages publish no such programme. Never give your Meta login to a site promising tokens.

faqs.q: How do I join the official waitlist?
faqs.a: Go to muse.ai and sign in with your Meta account. If a waitlist is offered for your country you will see it there. That is the only official route; nobody legitimate sells or swaps waitlist positions.

faqs.q: Can I use a VPN or a friend's foreign account to get Muse early?
faqs.a: We do not recommend it, and this page never teaches ways around the launch regions: using a service from a country where it has not launched can break Meta's terms and put your Meta account at risk. The safe route is the official waitlist.

faqs.q: When will Muse launch in my country?

faqs.q: What does the Cliché Cleaner do?
faqs.a: It scans your text for repeated stock phrases that can make writing feel formulaic — phrases like 'delve', 'rich tapestry', 'testament to' or 'pivotal role' — and suggests plainer wording in your own voice.

faqs.q: Does a flagged phrase prove AI wrote my text?
faqs.a: No. People use these phrases too. A flag only means the phrase is overused; whether to change it is an editing decision, not a verdict on authorship.

faqs.q: Is it free? Is my text uploaded?
faqs.a: Yes, it is free with no sign-up and runs in your browser; your text is not uploaded by this tool.

facts: Flags overused stock phrases and suggests plainer wording
A flagged phrase never proves how a text was written

faqs.q: What does the diff checker's similarity score mean?
faqs.a: It calculates word-level similarity between two texts you provide and highlights exactly which words were added, removed or kept. A lower similarity score means more of the wording was altered. It is a comparison aid, not a prediction of any detector's verdict.

faqs.q: Is this a plagiarism checker?
faqs.a: No. It compares two texts you paste against each other; it does not search the web or any database, and it cannot say where a text came from.

faqs.q: Is it free? Is my text uploaded?
faqs.a: Yes, it is free with no sign-up and the comparison runs in your browser.

facts: Word-level diff and similarity % between two texts you paste
